newsitem.title: USA: Friend seeks death row liver for King killer.
newsitem.headline: Friend seeks death row liver for King killer.

text.p: An art dealer is seeking potential liver donors among death row inmates in Texas, Florida and Georgia to save the life of James Earl Ray, Ray's brother Jerry said Friday.

Jerry Ray said the dealer, Arthur Deco, decided to help because James Earl Ray is dying of cirrhosis of the liver and cannot get on a national liver transplant list because of his age and other factors.
Ray, 68, has been serving a 99-year sentence in Tennessee since he confessed to shooting civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr. in Memphis, on April 4, 1968.
Although Ray's confession protected him from a possible death sentence, he recanted the statement and has asked repeatedly for a trial, but authorities have refused.
King's relatives have also sought a trial for Ray and the latest request is scheduled to be heard Feb. 20 in Shelby County criminal court in Memphis.
Deco, an art dealer and writer who interviewed Ray in prison and has sold some of his paintings, said he has sent about three dozen letters to inmates and plans to send more to California.
